items.action: Small boat used to carry passengers across the river between banks, or mixed cargo such as wine or sand; sometimes used for fishing.
items.gear: square sail or spiked sail

items.action: Flat-bottomed, keel-less boat, notable for not being built in a shipyard but on the riverbank.
Small wooden-box-shaped boat from Vila Praia de Âncora used for deep-sea, coastal and river fishing, handled by two men.
items.gear: small mast forward with a bastard lateen yard

items.action: Carried barrels of wine down the Douro to the Gaia wine cellars.
items.gear: square sail; long steering oar (espadela) worked from a raised platform aft

items.action: Boat from the Valbom area sailed on river and sea, used for fishing and for carrying goods and passengers between banks.
items.gear: long paddle-like oar instead of a rudder; small shelter (camareta) for passenger

items.action: Boats were named by their cargo: bakers' boat (barco das padeiras) and bacon-sellers' boat (barco das toucinheiras).
Douro boats classed by cargo like the Valboeiro; carried passengers on benches under a protective awning, steered by a long paddle instead of a rudder.
items.gear: awning, benches, pendant sail on forward mast

items.action: Different Poveira boat types served different fisheries: large lancha for hake, batel and small lancha for sardine and longline, caíco for whiting.
items.gear: espinel (longline); removable mast raked aft, trapezoidal sail; 4 to 5 oars per

items.action: Harvested and carried moliço (aquatic weed), also cargo and livestock, through the canals of the Ria de Aveiro.
items.conditions: very low sides and minimal draught suit the canals
items.gear: sail, towing line (sirga), pole (vara), large rudder

items.action: Annual regatta on the ria that still gathers more than twenty moliceiro boats.
Completely black, undecorated boat from Ílhavo, similar to the Moliceiro, usually crewed by three.
Used for sardine fishing, where sardines were picked and salted aboard; sailed fast and were sometimes raced in sporting regattas against one another.
items.gear: bastard lateen sail on foremast, small mizzen

items.action: Deep-sea fishing between Cabo da Roca and São Vicente; masts were lowered onto the benches and oars used during fishing work.
items.conditions: masts lowered onto benches during fishing
items.gear: two spritsails, oars
items.place: Sesimbra; Cabo da Roca to São Vicente

items.action: Elegant deep-sea fishing boat from Setúbal with schooner-like rig, bowsprit, continuous hull, wide mouth and two symmetrical masts raked slightly aft.
items.gear: two masts, bowsprit

items.action: Described as the most emblematic Tagus boat: heavy, bulging, with gaff mainsail, two decorated cabins, and a small boat towed behind for rowing the fragata along.
items.gear: stay, gaff mainsail, towed small boat with oars

items.action: Elegant, decorated cargo vessel of the late 19th century, like a large two-ended bateira, descended from a boat the Ílhavo people left on the Tagus.
items.gear: stay and lateen sail on strongly raked mast

items.action: Typical Tagus cargo carrier, keel-less and bulging but more elegant than the fragata, with false bulwarks and a hold with baskets for stowing cargo.
items.gear: one or two stay sails, quadrangular sail

items.action: Used for fishing and carrying people and cargo between the two river banks; side leeboards helped manoeuvring.
items.gear: large bastard lateen, small stay on bowsprit, side leeboards

items.action: Mainly carried people between the two Tagus banks, and also served Lisbon's markets; lateen-rigged and from the varino family.
items.gear: large bastard lateen, small stay
items.who: crew of two to three men

items.action: Normally carried cargo and passengers between the two banks; fast, single- or two-masted with bastard lateens.
items.gear: bastard lateen sails

items.action: Carried heavy cargo such as sand and stone for construction; a support boat with oars helped manoeuvring, and crew poled the boat in shallows.
items.gear: support boat, oars, large poles

items.action: Almost exclusively carried pine branches arriving from the south bank; decorated, with false bulwarks to stow cargo.
items.gear: long triangular lateen sail on short forward mast

items.action: Smaller Tagus boat with fragata-like hull, stem joined smoothly to the keel, usually with a large bastard lateen.
items.gear: large bastard lateen; some with stay sail

items.action: Smaller fragata-like boat whose main role was carrying cargo and transshipping goods between anchored ships.
Riba-Tejo boat began as a fishing craft, then gradually served as cargo and coastal trade vessel; steeply raked mast carried a long bastard lateen sail.
items.conditions: side espadelas helped manoeuvring and navigation in the Tejo's channels and creeks
items.gear: long latino bastardo sail; lateral espadelas

items.action: Praieira is a flat-bottomed, fully decked bateira-type boat with a large removable rudder that aids navigation of Tejo creeks and channels; waxed shelter aft stores utensils and rests crew.
items.conditions: navigating creeks and channels of the Tejo
items.gear: espicha sail, small stay, removable blade rudder

items.action: Fishermen used the Muleta do Seixal solely for the tarantanha fishing method; it had a wide flat bottom and a steeply forward-raked mast.
items.gear: tarantanha; raked mast with yard
items.who: fishermen of Seixal, Barreiro and Cascais

items.action: Caíque do Algarve is a typical vessel of the Algarve leeward coast with two diverging masts and two large lateen sails; some say it descends from discovery-era caravels.
items.gear: two lateen sails, diverging masts
items.place: Algarve, between Faro and Vila Real de Santo António

items.action: Reports say caíques sailed as far as Brazil and southern Angola; ashore, two water dogs reportedly guarded them while the crew was on land.
Olhão's Canoa do Espinel was meant for espinel line fishing, though sometimes it carried the catch between ports.
items.gear: espinel; two lateen sails; cane rudder

items.action: Enviada da Arte da Chávega, from Monte Gordo, also ferried the catch between offshore boats and land, giving it its name.
items.gear: four oars, two per side

items.action: Enviado do Atum of Vila Real de Santo António was used for tuna fishing and also carried the catch, hence its name.
items.gear: two diverging masts with lateen sails; oars

items.action: Baleeira do Pico was used for whale hunting on Pico and Faial; during the chase sails were lowered and part of the crew rowed.
items.gear: small lateen sail; 6 oars

items.action: During Semana do Mar, held at Faial in the first week of August, the Pico whaleboat can still be seen.
Azorean mackerel-fishing boat carried a crew who could use oars; a projecting cleat and pulley at the bow helped haul in the catch.
items.gear: 4 oars; bow pulley

items.action: After whales became scarce in mainland waters, whaling continued in Madeira and the Azores, using the Câmara de Lobos whaleboat in Madeira.
